body_html:
How to think about it

The Earth has a crust, mantle, outer core and inner core. The lithosphere is broken into plates that move on the softer asthenosphere, driven by mantle convection, ridge push and slab pull. Evidence for continental drift includes matching continents and fossils, seafloor spreading, magnetic striping and the age of the ocean floor.

At divergent boundaries plates move apart (mid-ocean ridges); at convergent boundaries they collide (subduction zones, trenches, volcanic arcs and mountains); at transform boundaries they slide past (faults). The Philippine Trench and Manila Trench are subduction zones that can cause large earthquakes and tsunamis.

Example

The seafloor is youngest at which feature?

New crust forms there.

Answer: the mid-ocean ridge

Example

What happens when oceanic crust meets continental crust?

Denser crust sinks.

Answer: the oceanic crust subducts

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the mantle is liquid.
  • Thinking continents move but the ocean floor does not.
  • Mixing up convergent and divergent boundaries.
